expectations.text: States ECC applicability correctly for this entity: as a government subsidiary, ECC-2:2024 is MANDATORY (not merely recommended)
expectations.evidence: The response never explicitly states that ECC-2:2024 is mandatory for a government subsidiary. It assumes compliance is needed throughout but does not make the applicability determination the assertion requires — no statement like 'ECC is mandatory (not recommended) for you' appears anywhere.

expectations.text: Describes ECC-2:2024's structure accurately: 4 domains (Governance; Defense; Resilience; Third-Party & Cloud), 28 subdomains, 108 main controls (+92 subcontrols), control IDs in domain-subdomain-control format — and does not invent specific control IDs
expectations.evidence: Only ISO 27001:2022's structure is described ('93 Annex A controls across four themes — Organizational, People, Physical, Technological'). ECC-2:2024's own structure (4 domains, 28 subdomains, 108 main controls + 92 subcontrols, control ID format) is never stated anywhere.

expectations.text: Gives a credible ISO mapping: ISO 27001:2022 Annex A covers much of Governance/Defense/Third-Party thematically, and certification evidence can be reused — but ISO certification does NOT constitute ECC compliance
expectations.evidence: 'organizations that hold a mature ISO 27001:2022 certification typically find that a large majority of ECC's operational and technical control objectives are already substantively covered... commonly estimated in the range of roughly 60–75% of ECC subcontrols in practice.' 'ISO 27001 certification is a third-party audit against an accredited certification body; it does not satisfy the NCA's own reporting/submission requirements.'

expectations.text: Names Saudi-specific deltas ISO does not satisfy: NCA compliance-tool reporting/self-assessment mechanics and NCA audits, Arabic-language governance artifacts where required, KSA residency/cloud rules for government data (CCC/CST), and OT/telework/data siblings (OTCC/TCC/DCC) where in scope
expectations.evidence: Covers NCA reporting/self-assessment obligations, CCC/CST residency, and OT/ICS controls, but Arabic-language governance artifacts are never mentioned anywhere, and telework (TCC) and data (DCC) control siblings are not named — only OT/ICS is addressed among the sibling frameworks.

expectations.text: Recommends the right process: map Annex A controls to ECC domains, gap-assess the uncovered ECC controls, and prepare NCA-facing evidence — structured as a gap table with evidence columns
expectations.evidence: Recommends a mapping exercise in narrative form ('Commission a formal control-mapping exercise: map your current ISO 27001:2022 SoA... against the full current text of NCA ECC-2:2024 domain by domain and subcontrol by subcontrol') but never structures this as an actual gap table with evidence columns — no table is produced.
